news.title: Russia Launches Massive Overnight Missile Attack on Kyiv
news.text: Russia carried out one of its largest missile and drone attacks on Ukraine's capital Kyiv on the night of July 2, 2026. Ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones rained down on the city for several hours, killing multiple people and causing significant damage to residential buildings. Emergency crews worked through the night digging through rubble to search for survivors. Many residents sheltered in subway stations as loud explosions shook the city. The attack has drawn strong international condemnation.

news.title: Iran Prepares for Supreme Leader Khamenei's State Funeral
news.text: Iran is preparing for the multi-day state funeral of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in an Israeli strike earlier this year. Delegations from nearly 100 countries, including heads of government, foreign ministers, and senior officials, are expected to attend. Iranian President Pezeshkian called on all Iranians to unite and attend the ceremonies to display national solidarity. Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guards issued fresh warnings to ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global oil shipping route, adding to tensions in the region.

news.title: Record-Breaking Heat Wave Grips the United States Ahead of July 4th
news.text: A massive heat dome has trapped more than half of the United States under dangerously high temperatures, making this July 4th potentially the hottest on record for millions of Americans. Over 185 million people are under heat alerts, including residents of Boston, New York City, Philadelphia, and Washington D.C. More than 300 temperature records are expected to be broken by Saturday. Authorities have urged people to stay hydrated, limit outdoor activity, and check on vulnerable neighbours during the extreme heat.

news.title: US Economy Adds Just 57,000 Jobs in June — Weakest in Years
news.text: The United States economy added only 57,000 jobs in June 2026, far below expectations and a worrying signal for the health of the labour market. Wage growth also remained below inflation for the third consecutive month, putting pressure on working households. Economists warn the data may push the Federal Reserve to reconsider its interest rate stance. The weak jobs report has sparked debate in Washington over economic policy and the long-term impact of recent tariff measures on employment.

news.title: India Gets Rs 52,000-Crore Defence Boost — DAC Approves Anti-Drone Systems and Missiles
news.text: India's Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) has approved a major Rs 52,000-crore defence procurement package that includes advanced anti-drone systems, air defence missiles, and naval equipment. The approval is part of India's ongoing effort to modernise its armed forces and strengthen its indigenous defence manufacturing sector. The move comes amid heightened regional security concerns and reflects India's push toward self-reliance in defence under the 'Aatmanirbhar Bharat' initiative.

news.title: India–Japan Summit 2026: Both Nations Pledge Deeper Economic and Strategic Ties
news.text: India and Japan held a high-level summit this week, reaffirming their commitment to deepening bilateral ties across trade, technology, and regional security. Trade Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that Japan and India are working together to promote industrial investment in India's Northeast region. The two nations also discussed cooperation in semiconductors, clean energy, and digital infrastructure. The summit signals a strengthening of the strategic partnership between Asia's two largest democracies.

news.title: Vatican Declares Society of St. Pius X in Schism After Unauthorised Bishop Consecrations
news.text: The Vatican responded sharply after the traditionalist Society of St. Pius X consecrated four new bishops without the Pope's approval — a direct violation of Catholic canon law. The Vatican formally declared the society in schism and excommunicated the newly consecrated bishops and associated priests. The move marks one of the most significant rifts in the Catholic Church in recent years and has reignited debate over traditionalist movements within the Church.

news.title: FIFA World Cup 2026: USA, Spain, Portugal, and France Advance to Round of 16
news.text: The FIFA World Cup 2026 Round of 32 has delivered thrilling action this week. The United States defeated Bosnia and Herzegovina 2–0 to set up a Round of 16 clash with Belgium. Spain demolished Austria 3–0, Portugal edged past Croatia 2–1, and France continued their strong form with a 3–0 win over Sweden. Germany suffered a dramatic exit, losing on penalties to Paraguay. Argentina and Lionel Messi face Cape Verde on July 3, with Messi currently leading the Golden Boot race with six goals.

news.title: Pakistan Roof Collapse at Lahore Tutoring Centre Kills Children
news.text: A tragic roof collapse at a tutoring centre on the outskirts of Lahore, Pakistan, claimed the lives of several children on July 1, 2026. Rescue teams worked urgently to pull survivors from the debris as grief-stricken families gathered at the site. The incident has raised serious concerns about building safety standards and the structural integrity of educational facilities across the country. Authorities have launched an investigation and announced immediate inspections of similar structures.

didYouKnow.title: FIFA World Cup Smart Ball
didYouKnow.content: The FIFA World Cup 2026 is using a revolutionary 'smart ball' technology for the first time. The ball contains a sensor that sends positional data 500 times per second to help referees and VAR officials make faster and more accurate offside and goal-line decisions.

didYouKnow.title: USA's 250th Birthday
didYouKnow.content: The United States is celebrating its 250th birthday on July 4, 2026. Interestingly, while Americans celebrate independence on July 4th, the Continental Congress actually voted to declare independence on July 2nd, 1776. John Adams predicted July 2nd would be the day celebrated forever — he was off by two days!

didYouKnow.title: Strait of Hormuz
didYouKnow.content: The Strait of Hormuz, currently at the centre of global tensions, is only 33 kilometres wide at its narrowest point. Despite its small size, roughly one-fifth of the world's entire oil supply and a significant portion of global liquefied natural gas passes through it daily, making it the world's most strategically important waterway.

didYouKnow.title: Cabo Verde at World Cup 2026
didYouKnow.content: Cabo Verde — an island nation of just 500,000 people — have made history at the FIFA World Cup 2026 by becoming the smallest nation ever to reach the knockout stage. Their 40-year-old goalkeeper Vozinha is also making history as one of the oldest goalkeepers ever to play in a World Cup knockout match.

didYouKnow.title: Ocean Exploration
didYouKnow.content: Despite covering more than 70% of Earth's surface, humans have explored less than 0.001% of the ocean floor — roughly the same area as Rhode Island, the smallest US state. We actually have more detailed maps of the surface of the Moon than we do of the deep sea floor.
